items.title: A 5-character token yields "…" plus its last 4 characters
covers: AC2: token longer than 4 characters (just above the limit)
items.reason: AC2 switches rule at 4 characters; 5 is the shortest token that shows its end. Guards an off-by-one (`>=` vs `>`) that would hide the hint or show the whole token.

items.title: A 4-character token yields "…" alone, never the whole token
covers: AC2: token with 1 to 4 characters shows "…" alone (upper edge)
items.reason: AC2 forbids showing a whole token; with a 4-character token "the last 4 characters" is the whole token, so this is the edge where a naive implementation leaks it.

items.title: A 1-character token yields "…" alone
covers: AC2: token with 1 to 4 characters shows "…" alone (lower edge)
items.reason: Lower edge of AC2's 1–4 range: one character is still a token (not "no token"), so the hint must be `"…"`, not `null` and not the character itself.

items.title: A subscription registered without a token has tokenHint null
covers: AC2: tokenHint is null when the subscription has no token
items.reason: AC2's third branch. The Webhooks API accepts a POST without a token (only the client UI requires one), so such rows exist and must not get `"…"` or crash the mapping.

items.title: A subscription registered with an empty token has tokenHint null
covers: AC2: 0-character token is outside 1–4, treated as no token
items.reason: Just below AC2's 1–4 range: an empty string is not a 1–4 character token, so the literal reading (and the recorded decision) is "no token" → `null`, not `"…"`.

reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 8/10, sol 7/10; 3 finding(s) stand, 1 note(s).

items.reason: AC5 says the registered token is still the token the Webhooks API sends with each webhook call. Only storage is checked (TC-HINT-1-14); delivery is in Open questions because it 'needs an order to reach OrderPaid on the test stack'. It doesn't: OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEventHandler only calls retriever.GetSubscriptionsOfType(OrderPaid) and sender.SendAll, and the functional fixture runs real RabbitMQ and already swaps services. Add a functional case: register (POST /api/webhooks/, X-Test-User fresh, token 'fake-token-for-tests-9z8y', url 'https://receiver.test/webhook', event OrderPaid) -> 201; publish an OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEvent (or resolve and invoke the handler) with the HttpClient primary handler replaced by a recording handler; expect exactly one POST to https://receiver.test/webhook whose X-eshop-whtoken header equals 'fake-token-for-tests-9z8y' (the full token, not its hint).

AC5 explicitly requires the entered token to be sent with webhook calls. Checking its database value does not verify the outgoing header, and this defined requirement cannot be deferred as an open question. Explicitly map reusable sender coverage, such as SenderPostsPayloadAndTokenToEveryReceiver, alongside TC-HINT-1-14, or plan an observable receiver assertion that X-eshop-whtoken equals the registered token.

The expected recorded argument and invocation count are state inside ConfigurableGrantUrlTester, not a documented public interface. Replace that assertion with an observable HTTP grant exchange: a controlled receiver verifies the exact X-eshop-whtoken header and returns the required grant response; assert POST 201 and the unchanged database token.

'the grant tester was called once with token ...' depends on a recorder that is a singleton shared by every test on the functional host (ConfigurableGrantUrlTester is registered AddSingleton). State that the case checks exactly one recorded call for grant URL https://receiver.test/check and hook URL https://receiver.test/webhook made during this test (or that the recorder is reset per test), so two engineers write the same assertion.

subject: test-planner
reason: Plan unchanged except for one open question. The hint rule and its boundaries, the field and status-code checks and the registration and grant checks stay functional against the Webhooks API; the client's Token column and the unauthenticated read stay e2e on the test stack.

excluded.reason: not touched by the story

excluded.item: WebhookSubscription entity and schema changes
excluded.reason: unchanged by design; only the stored token value is checked (TC-HINT-1-14)

excluded.reason: the story says it is shown nowhere new; there is no new UI to test

excluded.reason: not defined by the story (see Open questions); TC-HINT-1-11 checks only the status and that nothing leaks

items.title: A 5-character token yields "…" plus its last 4 characters
covers: AC2: token longer than 4 characters (just above the limit)
items.reason: AC2 switches rule at 4 characters; 5 is the shortest token that shows its end. Guards an off-by-one (`>=` vs `>`) that would hide the hint or show the whole token.

items.title: A 4-character token yields "…" alone, never the whole token
covers: AC2: token with 1 to 4 characters shows "…" alone (upper edge)
items.reason: AC2 forbids showing a whole token; with a 4-character token "the last 4 characters" is the whole token, so this is the edge where a naive implementation leaks it.

items.title: A 1-character token yields "…" alone
covers: AC2: token with 1 to 4 characters shows "…" alone (lower edge)
items.reason: Lower edge of AC2's 1–4 range: one character is still a token (not "no token"), so the hint must be `"…"`, not `null` and not the character itself.

items.title: A subscription registered without a token has tokenHint null
covers: AC2: tokenHint is null when the subscription has no token
items.reason: AC2's third branch. The Webhooks API accepts a POST without a token (only the client UI requires one), so such rows exist and must not get `"…"` or crash the mapping.

items.title: A subscription registered with an empty token has tokenHint null
covers: AC2: 0-character token is outside 1–4, treated as no token
items.reason: Just below AC2's 1–4 range: an empty string is not a 1–4 character token, so the literal reading (and the recorded decision) is "no token" → `null`, not `"…"`.

items.title: List and single answers carry tokenHint instead of token and keep id, type, date, destUrl and userId with their values
covers: AC1: GET /api/webhooks and GET /api/webhooks/{id} have no token, have tokenHint
AC2: token longer than 4 characters
AC3: id, type, date, destUrl, userId returned as today
AC3: status codes unchanged (200)
items.reason: AC1 is the point of the story (neither read endpoint may expose a token) and AC3 says the new response model must not drop or rename existing fields; the webhooks client depends on `date` and `destUrl`. Both endpoints map their own response, so each is checked. The body is inspected as raw JSON at the functional layer (Webhooks API in-process against real Postgres) because deserializing into a typed model would hide a leftover `token` property.

items.title: GET /api/webhooks/{id} of another user's subscription still returns 404 and no hint
covers: AC3: 404 for a subscription that is not the caller's
items.reason: AC3 explicitly keeps the 404 for someone else's subscription; the rewritten handler must not start returning the response model (even with only a hint) to a non-owner.

items.title: GET /api/webhooks without a bearer token is still refused with 401
covers: AC3: status codes unchanged (unauthenticated read)
items.reason: AC3 keeps every status code; the read endpoints must still require identity, otherwise even hints of everyone's subscriptions would be readable. The functional host replaces authentication, so this runs as an API call on the test stack.

items.title: After registering on /add-webhook, the home page Token column shows "…" and the last 4 characters
covers: AC4: Token column shows the hint, never a whole token
AC5: /add-webhook registration behaves as today
items.reason: AC4 is the visible half of the story and AC5 says registering through the client still works; one journey through the real WebApp covers the client model, the razor binding and the API answer together, which only the e2e layer can.

items.title: The home page Token column shows "None" for a webhook without a token and hints for the others
covers: AC4: Token column shows "None" when the webhook has no token
AC4: seeded rows show hints, never whole tokens
items.reason: AC4's "None" branch can't be produced through `/add-webhook` (it requires a token), so it is seeded; seeding also lets one view prove every row shows a hint (long and short tokens), not just the one just registered.

items.title: POST /api/webhooks still stores the exact token and sends it to the grant URL
covers: AC5: POST /api/webhooks and the grant check behave as today
AC5: the token entered is the token stored
items.reason: AC5: hiding the token on reads must not change what is checked or stored. The grant check is observed as the HTTP exchange it really is (the real `GrantUrlTesterService` sends `OPTIONS` with `X-eshop-whtoken` and needs the same header back), so a token replaced by its hint anywhere on the registration path would show up in the header or in the row, not in a test double's internal state.

items.title: A rejected grant check still returns 400 and stores nothing
covers: AC5: the grant check behaves as today (rejected grant)
items.reason: AC5 keeps the grant check exactly as today; this existing error is the only failure path of registration and must survive the change unchanged.

items.title: An OrderPaid webhook call carries the registered token in full
covers: AC5: the token entered at registration is the token the Webhooks API sends with each webhook call
items.reason: AC5 requires that the registered token is still the one sent with each webhook call; checking the stored value alone does not prove the outgoing `X-eshop-whtoken` header. The OrderPaid handler only reads subscriptions of that type and calls the sender, so the call can be triggered in-process on the functional host (real Postgres) without an order on the test stack; the e2e layer would need a whole order flow this story does not touch.

items.title: A token ending in a non-BMP character keeps the surrogate pair whole in its hint
covers: AC2: token longer than 4 characters, counted as characters, not UTF-16 code units
items.reason: The hint counts text elements; slicing the last 4 UTF-16 code units would split a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane and return a broken surrogate. Guards a regression to code-unit slicing.

items.title: Register with an empty Token box shows "A token is needed to register a webhook." next to the form
covers: Expected: after step 4 the page says, next to the form, that a token is needed to register a webhook
Steps to Reproduce 1-4
Actual (regression: no message shown)
items.reason: This is the bug itself: before the fix, Register with an empty Token box changed nothing on the page. It must run through the browser (e2e) because the defect is what the user sees after a click in a Blazor page; no API or unit layer reaches the rendered message. Kept separate from TC-BUG-52-02 so a missing message and an unwanted registration fail as distinct cases.

items.title: Register with an empty Token box registers no webhook
covers: Expected: no webhook is registered
Implementation Notes: empty token -> no POST
items.reason: The ticket requires that an empty token registers nothing; if the guard were removed, the page could send a subscription with an empty token to the Webhooks API. Checked at e2e because the trigger is the page's form; the page is server-rendered Blazor, so the request would leave the server, not the browser; the outcome is therefore checked in the user's registered-webhooks list on the home page and through the Webhooks API.

items.title: Register with a token registers the webhook and returns to the home page as before
covers: Expected: Register with a token in the box behaves exactly as today
Implementation Notes: token present -> navigate home on success
items.reason: The fix must not change the path with a token: success still registers the `OrderPaid` webhook and navigates home. A regression here (for example the guard firing for a filled box, or a stale message blocking submit) would break the client's only registration flow, which only the browser flow on the test stack exercises end to end (page -> Webhooks API -> grant check against the client's `/check`).

items.title: After the empty-token message, entering a token and registering succeeds
covers: Expected: Register with a token in the box behaves exactly as today
Expected: message for the empty Token box (recovery after it)
items.reason: The new message is state on the page; the ticket requires that Register with a token behaves exactly as today, including right after the user saw the message. If the message state blocked or altered the next submit, the user who follows the message's advice could not register. Only the browser flow shows this sequence.
